title: Full-Cohort Causal RMST under Unknown Weak Entry: Minimax Risk and Honest Interval Length
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Math referee passed with no findings; novelty-positioning finding remains unrepaired. Projected paper-score ceiling 7.0 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The delivered statements establish matching minimax orders for absolute risk and finite-sample honest interval length; the framing contains no stale one-sided or conjectural frontier claim. Smooth weak-overlap phase transitions already appear in [Mou et al., Corollary 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.06240), so the contribution is specifically the learned-entry construction and normalized joint-likelihood converse in this truncation experiment. The theorem requires supplied endpoint powers and event smoothness, and its causal scope consists of randomized armwise marginal problems without censoring or covariates; adaptation and broader causal inference are not delivered. The conservative interval certificate can return the entire parameter range at moderate sample sizes, and the package supplies no implementation or coverage-length evidence establishing practical usefulness. The inaccessible boundary results in [Efromovich (2004)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378375803002027) require theorem-level source verification before historical novelty positioning can be settled, but their abstract does not establish containment. These constraints limit the projected paper score to 7.0 despite the completed matching rate theorem. proof_attempt_summary: D0 completed the matching finite-n minimax absolute-risk and 90%-honest connected-interval-length frontier, including the critical logarithm, a total same-record learned-entry procedure, and normalized original-joint converses. Maximality strengthened entry shapes from Hölder to continuous normalized envelope-bounded laws; the mathematical referee passed with no findings. tldr: The full-cohort causal RMST contrast has matching minimax absolute-error risk and maximal expected length of connected intervals that are honest at level \(0.90\) for every finite \(n\). Event and entry densities have public endpoint powers and unknown normalized shapes in \([1/2,2]\); event shapes are \(s\)-Hölder, while entry shapes need only be continuous. The explicit profile is \(r_n=\min\{1,\sqrt{(1+J_{\rho-\gamma}(n^{-1/(\rho+\gamma+2s)}))/n}\}\). Its fixed-parameter orders are \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(\rho>\gamma\), \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) for \(\rho=\gamma\), and \(n^{-(\rho+s)/(\rho+\gamma+2s)}\) for \(\rho<\gamma\). A total finite observable procedure learns arm-specific entry ratios from the same selected pairs, extrapolates the smooth event boundary, and attains this profile; normalized original-joint alternatives prove matching lower bounds against all randomized procedures. Constants are uniform on compact public-parameter sets. Regular efficiency and generic weak-overlap transitions remain credited baselines; historical priority is not asserted.
gap: Accessible regular truncation theory identifies full-cohort means and supplies square-integrable gradients or product-limit CLTs; accessible weak-overlap and fixed-interval hazard results do not contain the combined joint selected-pair, unknown-entry, normalized full-origin RMST minimax-risk and honest-connected-interval frontier. Efromovich (2004) has relevant distribution-estimation boundary results, but its full theorem text is inaccessible, so a theorem-level exclusion and any first-ever priority claim are unsupported.
fill: The field-tier kernel evaluates \((R_n,H_n)\) throughout the supplied \(\mathcal M(\rho,\gamma,s)\). A rectangle conditional sample, a shared-pilot stochastic certificate, boundary reproduction and original-joint testing are the construction handles. Rate exponents and logarithms are derived outputs. Their exact evaluation, root-\(n\) boundary, matched normalized lower construction and finite honest interval form the headline theorem after Open-ended Question 1 is solved.
